title: Commons domain modules import nothing outward

facts.note: Commons domain tree identified from the path.
File must carry a layer segment; files with no layer segment are outside the rule.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.

Import-graph observer: any import (existing or newly changed) in a commons domain module whose resolved target lies in the application/ or integration/ layer; bare npm specifiers excluded. Path/layer/file-kind facts alone cannot resolve import targets. A bun_clean_architecture_detector finding is an optional signal/evidence, not a prerequisite.

fires: A module under commons/domain/ has an import (new or pre-existing) resolving into commons application/.
A module under shared/domain/ imports a helper from the integration/ layer (e.g. a persistence or transport adapter).
A module under commons/domain/ or shared/domain/ imports an outer-layer type as a temporary shortcut to make a test pass.
doesNotFire: A test file under commons/domain/ imports application code (tests are not scanned).
A file in a vendored or build directory.
A commons domain module imports a bare npm specifier (outside the project graph).
A file whose path carries no layer segment.
An application/ or integration/ module importing from commons domain (inward direction).

given: A source module under a `commons/domain/` or `shared/domain/` tree
when: it has an import resolving into the commons `application/` or `integration/` layer
then: Remove the outward import: commons domain MUST NOT import application or integration code; dependencies point inward only.
prefer: Move genuinely domain-owned data or behavior into domain.
Invert an outer capability behind a domain-facing port.

During GREEN: prefer existing domain types, functions, and ports; introduce a new port only when the current behavior requires the domain to request an outer capability, and keep it as narrow as the acceptance requires.
avoid: Importing outward as a temporary shortcut.
Moving unrelated application or integration behavior into domain.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file with no layer segment is outside the rule, not in violation.
why: The domain is the centre holding the rules and must not know what orchestrates or transports them; an outward import makes the rules unusable without the machinery, first seen as a domain test needing a database.
evidence: Commons domain imports no application or integration code: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no import from a commons domain module resolving into application/ or integration/.
verifier_detail: Scope: modules under `commons/domain/` or `shared/domain/` trees (term commons_domain: the shared centre holding rules).
Outbound import (term outbound_import): an import whose resolved target lies in the application or integration layer; applies to existing as well as newly changed imports.
Skip test files and vendored/build directories entirely.
Do not layer-check bare npm specifiers; they resolve outside the project graph.
Files with no layer segment in their path are out of scope, not violations.
audit: Source summary: Flags an import from a commons domain module that resolves into the application or integration layer.

sharedNodes.text: Do not broaden: do not invent a future-proof abstraction. Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.
